prompt:
Character sprite sheet for a modern 2.5D role-playing game that places hand-made pixel-art character sprites into a three-dimensional diorama world. Classic 16-bit-era field-sprite pixel art: each figure about 48 art pixels tall, every art pixel a crisp square block of the same size on one regular grid (about 5 by 5 image pixels), as if a small game sprite were enlarged without smoothing; no anti-aliasing, no blur, no soft gradients, no texture noise, no glow. The figures are seen from slightly above (about 15 degrees), exactly as in the pose sheet. Clean readable shapes, 3 to 4 shades per material with gently hue-shifted ramps (greens shift towards teal in the shadows and yellow-green in the highlights, the red scarf towards crimson in the shadows, the dark fur from deep blue-grey to warm grey), light from the upper left, a one-pixel very dark warm-brown outline (not pure black) around the whole figure, a few lighter outline pixels on the lit side. A readable face: the broad white stripe from the nose over the forehead, the dark stripe through each eye, small shiny dark eyes with a one-pixel highlight, a black nose tip, a small friendly smile. About 28 colours in total.

The first reference image is a pose sheet rendered from a 3D model: copy its layout exactly, with the same 8 walking frames in the top row and the same 4 front-facing frames in the bottom row, at the same positions and the same scale, with the same body poses and the same leg positions in every frame. The second reference image shows the costume and the proportions of the character: take only the costume, the colours of the clothes and the proportions from it; drawing style, resolution and palette follow this description.

Layout: Top row: 8 frames of a smooth walk cycle walking to the right, side view, following the leg positions of the pose sheet (left heel touches down, weight down, legs passing, up, right heel touches down, weight down, legs passing, up); the body bobs slightly, the free arm swings opposite to the legs, the back end of the scarf flutters behind, the parcel stays under the near arm in every frame. Bottom row: 4 frames facing the viewer, feet as in the pose sheet: 1 standing relaxed, eyes open, mouth closed; 2 exactly the same pose with both eyes closed (blink); 3 waving with the free paw raised high, paw tilted outwards, cheerful open mouth; 4 the same wave with the paw tilted inwards. All 12 figures at exactly the same scale, evenly spaced with clear empty space between them, the feet of each row on one baseline.

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

Isolated on a fully transparent background, no ground, no shadows, no glow, no frame borders, no grid lines. No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

Prop sprite sheet for the same modern 2.5D role-playing game as the reference image: hand-made pixel-art sprites of harbour props that stand as flat billboards in a three-dimensional diorama world. Drawn in exactly the same pixel-art style, pixel size and palette mood as the reference sprite sheet (about 5 by 5 image pixels per art pixel): every art pixel a crisp square block of the same size on one regular grid, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no soft gradients, no texture noise, 3 to 5 gently hue-shifted shades per material, light from the upper left, a one-pixel very dark warm-brown outline around each object, a few lighter outline pixels on the lit side. Seen from slightly above (about 15 degrees), so the tops of the barrel and the crates are just visible as narrow surfaces. Use the reference only for style, palette mood and pixel scale; do not draw the badger.

Layout: two rows, every object at the same pixel scale as the reference (the badger in the reference is 1 metre tall), each object standing on one baseline per row, evenly spaced with clear empty space between them. Top row, left to right: (1) a weathered wooden barrel with dark iron hoops, 0.9 m tall; (2) a stack of three wooden crates, two on the bottom and one on top, 1.2 m tall; (3) a single small wooden crate, 0.5 m tall; (4) a coil of thick hemp rope lying flat on the ground, 0.7 m across; (5) a small heap of brown fishing net with round cork floats, 0.4 m tall; (6) a tuft of wild grass with a few tiny white flowers, 0.3 m tall; (7) a tuft of tall pale sea grass, 0.4 m tall. Bottom row: (8) to (11) a white-and-grey seagull flying to the right, side view, four frames of one wing flap (wings high up, wings level, wings low down, wings level), wingspan 0.9 m, the body at the same height in all four frames; (12) the same seagull standing, side view facing right.

The props belong to the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk (only the props, not the scene; even neutral lighting on the props, the game lights them).

Isolated on a fully transparent background, no ground, no shadows, no glow, no frame borders, no grid lines. No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

Texture sheet for a modern 2.5D role-playing game whose three-dimensional diorama world is covered with hand-made pixel-art textures. Sixteen square surface textures arranged in an exact 4 by 4 grid of equal squares, separated by straight, even gutters of pure black (#000000), with a pure black border around the whole sheet. Every square is filled edge to edge with one flat surface material, seen straight on (orthographic, no perspective, no objects, no frame, no vignette). Pixel art: every square is 64 by 64 art pixels, every art pixel a crisp square block of the same size on one regular grid (about 3.5 by 3.5 image pixels), as if a small game texture were enlarged without smoothing; no anti-aliasing, no blur, no photographic detail, no fine noise. Classic 16-bit-era pixel-art technique: clear readable shapes, 4 to 5 shades per material with gently hue-shifted ramps, every stone, slate and plank with a one-pixel lighter top edge and a one-pixel darker bottom edge, dark one-pixel joints. Even overall brightness across each square, no light falloff and no baked shadow across the square, so that each texture tiles seamlessly: the pattern continues across the left/right and top/bottom edges without seams. Muted, slightly desaturated colours. Scale: one square covers 1.6 by 1.6 metres.
Row 1, left to right: (1) quay paving: large irregular rectangular grey granite flagstones, about 18 by 12 art pixels each, in staggered rows with dark joints, a few cracks and tiny moss spots; (2) rough fieldstone wall: grey-beige rectangular stones of varied length in horizontal courses with darker mortar joints; (3) dark grey dressed stone blocks in horizontal courses, larger and smoother; (4) dark blue-grey slate roof tiles in overlapping horizontal rows.
Row 2: (5) weathered warm-brown wooden planks running horizontally, grain lines and a few nail heads; (6) dark tarred wooden planks running horizontally, almost black-brown; (7) white-painted wooden boards running horizontally, slightly worn, thin dark seams; (8) red-painted wooden boards running horizontally, slightly worn, thin dark seams.
Row 3: (9) short grass and moss, muted olive green with tiny lighter blades and a few tiny pale flowers; (10) grey-brown coastal rock face with angular facets and cracks; (11) pale beach sand with small pebbles; (12) dark wet stone blocks with green algae.
Row 4: (13) coarse twisted hemp rope strands running diagonally, beige-brown; (14) dark iron plate with rivets and small rust patches; (15) weathered whitewashed lime plaster with faint grey stains; (16) wooden deck planks running vertically with dark gaps between them.
The materials are for a small stone fishing harbour on a fictional island in a northern sea (only the materials, not the scene).
No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.
Image format: square 1:1.
